note: Answer-to-served-distractor distances as the battery stood BEFORE closeness-ranked selection: commit 72ffdb3, the last commit before the escalate-the-quiz batch, whose selectDistractors samples the wrong options uniformly from each family's grammar. The plan and the docs call that pre-batch state v10, which is where this file's name comes from; the generator constant in that commit reads scene-families-v8. The tuples were re-measured on 2026-08-26 with the corrected coordinate-based metric (one position per board coordinate, crease guides as atoms only), so they are comparable with what scripts/scene-family-verify.ts reports today. Lexicographic (positions, atoms).
seedStream: <familyId>:<seed> for seeds 0-199, the bucket-free stream the verifier has always used
percentileRule: nearest rank over lexicographically sorted (positions, atoms) tuples: sorted[min(n-1, ceil(n*fraction)-1)]
distanceSource: the five non-answer options of the final shuffled puzzle, never copied candidate metadata
howThisWasRegenerated: git archive 72ffdb3 | tar -x -C <scratch>/v10   (read-only; the v10 selector is not in the working tree)
cp <repo>/src/items/scene-distance.ts <scratch>/v10/src/items/scene-distance.ts   (the metric changes, the measured population does not)

in <scratch>/v10, for every SCENE_FAMILY_IDS family and every seed 0-199: generateSceneFamilyCandidate(familyId, seededRng('scene-family-verify-v1', `${familyId}:${seed}`)) -- the v10 generator takes no bucket argument
for each candidate, measure sceneEditDistance(option, options[answerIndex]) for every option except the answer: 200 seeds x 5 distractors = 1000 tuples per family

assign each family's 1000 tuples to every `${familyId}:${band}:${difficultyBucket}` key that eligibleFamiliesForBand(CURRENT_FAMILY_PROMOTION_REGISTRY, band) enables at 72ffdb3, withdrawals ignored exactly as the verifier ignores them
take the nearest-rank p50 and p90 of each key's tuples

keysNotCarried.composed-transform-v2:composition:compos: No v10 baseline. At 72ffdb3 the family is composed-transform-v1, and v11 both renamed it and deepened its grammar with the two token turns, so its d4 population is not the same population. For the record, v10's composed-transform-v1 measured p50 (2, 2) and p90 (5, 21).
keysNotCarried.every other key the current registry ser: compositional-analogy-d4, parallel-evolution-d3, parallel-evolution-d4, fold-punch-d5, visual-set-algebra-d5 and composed-transform-d5 did not exist at v10, and neither did the two d6 buckets added on 2026-08-26, composed-transform-d6 and transformation-machine-d6. The verifier reports their percentiles with comparable: false and invents no baseline for them.

withdrawnKeysNote: Keys that once had a v10 baseline and are no longer served, kept with the numbers they were recorded with. A withdrawal is a normal event and must leave a record: deleting the row would make the gate green by forgetting, and the aggregate no-regression comparison runs over the keys still in "keys" either way. scripts/scene-family-verify.ts fails if a key appears in both objects, or if a key listed here turns up in a run.

containment-analogy-v2:constraint-spatia.note: Same family, same bucket, same v10 generator path; only the band label moved from composition to constraint-spatial during this batch.
containment-analogy-v2:constraint-spatia.withdrawnReason: containment-analogy-v2 was withdrawn from every band on 2026-08-26 on the human pilot's notation evidence (src/items/family-promotion.ts, data/pilot/README.md), so no run of scripts/scene-family-verify.ts measures this key any more. The numbers are kept exactly as they were recorded rather than deleted: the record of what the key measured is evidence, and a baseline file that quietly loses rows cannot be audited. The verifier skips it in the no-regression comparison and fails if the key is ever served again without this row moving back into "keys".
